domain_title: Popular Sovereignty and the People’s Branch
research_domain_title: Popular Sovereignty, Direct Democracy, and Judicial Accountability
note: Major constitutional doctrine architecture. Designs the Sovereign People as a constitutionally organized fourth branch with reserved powers. Federal initiatives, federal recall, fixed Supreme Court terms, and a third Article V pathway would require constitutional amendment and legal drafting (legal remains 0%). Illustrative thresholds (signature %, ratification %, term lengths) are design parameters — not locked text. No ordinary partisan recall of Supreme Court justices. Direct democracy is bounded by the same constitutional rights floor as every other branch.

problem.summary: Judicial independence is essential to protect unpopular persons from powerful majorities. Independence cannot mean freedom from enforceable ethics, lifetime ideological control, undisclosed conflicts, unreviewable recusal, unexplained emergency orders, partisan vacancy manipulation, or immunity from meaningful public accountability. The system must protect courts from political retaliation without protecting judges from accountability.

governing_principle.text: The people are not merely voters who periodically choose rulers. They are the continuing sovereign authority of the republic, retaining direct constitutional powers to propose, approve, reject, recall, review, and reform their government.

central_declaration.text: All governmental authority originates in the people and remains held in trust for them. Elections do not surrender that authority for the duration of a term. The people retain peaceful, structured, and constitutionally protected powers to propose laws, reject laws, recall officials, audit institutions, amend constitutions, and reform every branch of government.

peoples_court_declaration.text: The judiciary belongs neither to judges nor to political parties. It is the People’s Court: independent enough to protect rights, limited enough not to govern in place of the people, transparent enough to earn trust, and accountable enough that corruption, incapacity, or abuse of office can never hide behind judicial independence.

four_branches.label: The four branches
four_branches.note: The People’s Branch is the fourth branch in structure and the first source of authority. Legislature, executive, and judiciary exercise delegated powers; the people retain sovereign power to restructure the delegation.

branches.name: Judicial Branch
branches.role: Adjudicates disputes and protects constitutional rights

branches.name: People’s Branch (The Sovereign People)
branches.role: Retains ultimate authority to propose, reject, recall, amend, audit, and restructure government

four_branches.operating_mode: The People’s Branch would not maintain a permanent bureaucracy comparable to the executive. It would operate through elections, petitions, referendums, citizen assemblies, public audits, and constitutional conventions.

current_law_baselines.note: Descriptive baselines for design; not claims that Constitutional Capitalism has already amended the Constitution.

items.text: The Supreme Court’s power of judicial review was confirmed in Marbury v. Madison (1803); the Court’s own account states that while judicial review was anticipated, it is not explicitly provided in the Constitution and was confirmed in that decision.
NCSL reports that 24 states have a statewide citizen initiative process; there is no comparable national citizen-initiative lawmaking system under the current federal Constitution.
NCSL reports that 19 states allow recall elections of state officials; federal officials are not removable by voter recall under the current U.S. Constitution.
Article V provides amendment proposal by Congress or by convention on state applications, with ratification by the states; it does not provide a direct national citizen-petition route to the ballot.

Article III’s Good Behavior framework has been understood to support life tenure during good behavior for federal judges; durable fixed active Supreme Court terms would likely require constitutional amendment.
The Supreme Court issued its first formal Code of Conduct for Justices in November 2023; Constitutional Capitalism proposes going further with enforceable procedures and external review.
Federal judges are generally removable by impeachment and conviction, not by ordinary voter disagreement with rulings.

reserved_powers.title: Citizen initiative
reserved_powers.summary: Citizens could propose local ordinances, state statutes, state constitutional amendments, federal statutes, and federal constitutional amendments through verified procedures.

reserved_powers.title: Referendum
reserved_powers.summary: Citizens could require a public vote before certain enacted laws take effect — automatic for specified major decisions, petition-triggered, or required for constitutional changes, major public-asset transfers, extraordinary public debt, and laws altering elections or initiative rights.

reserved_powers.title: Citizen veto
reserved_powers.summary: Citizens could collect signatures during a defined period to suspend a contested law and place it before voters. Emergency laws could take temporary effect but expire unless ratified.

reserved_powers.title: Recall
reserved_powers.summary: Citizens could recall local officials, state legislators, governors, elected prosecutors, certain elected judges, and — under a new federal constitutional structure — members of Congress. Recall requires substantial thresholds and must not become a permanent campaign against every difficult decision. Ordinary partisan recall of Supreme Court justices is rejected.
safeguards: one recall attempt per term absent serious misconduct

reserved_powers.title: Constitutional initiative — People’s Amendment Process
reserved_powers.summary: A third Article V pathway allowing citizens to propose constitutional amendments without requiring the institutions being reformed to volunteer their own loss of power.

illustrative_design_parameters.note: Illustrative only — not locked constitutional text; require research, modeling of turnout effects, and legal drafting.
proposal_to_ballot: verified signatures from perhaps 5% of eligible voters nationally
minimum participation thresholds in at least two-thirds of the states
two separate national votes in different general-election cycles
ratification: at least 60% of the national popular vote
majority approval in at least three-fifths of the states

reserved_powers.design_goal: Easier than the current process, still difficult enough to prevent temporary passion from casually rewriting the Constitution.

reserved_powers.title: Citizen-triggered constitutional convention
reserved_powers.summary: Citizens could petition states to demand a limited convention on a defined subject, with safeguards against an uncontrolled convention.
safeguards: proposed amendments return to the people
nothing takes effect without supermajority ratification

reserved_powers.title: Citizen audit and investigation
reserved_powers.summary: A sufficient verified petition could require a public audit, inspector-general review, legislative hearing, conflict-of-interest investigation, public report, or examination of an agency, contract, court administration, or public body — so the people need not wait for political leadership to investigate itself.

rights_floor.distinction: The people may reorganize government and expand rights through democratic action. They may not use a temporary majority to strip another person of fundamental constitutional protection.
prohibited_ballot_uses: deny voting rights to a disfavored group
repeal the inherent dignity of any person
rights_floor.court_role: Courts retain authority to enforce that floor. A simple majority may not overturn every judicial decision or reverse an individual defendant’s case by plebiscite.

active_terms.proposal: 18-year nonrenewable active Supreme Court terms; one regularly scheduled appointment every two years; senior judicial status after active service; no retirement-timing manipulation; continuity without lifetime control.
active_terms.effect: Each presidential term would ordinarily receive two appointments.

judicial_accountability_council.summary: Independent constitutional body that does not allow any single president, Congress, party, or Court to appoint a majority.
composition_includes: retired judges selected by multiple methods
citizens chosen through a civic lottery
investigates: intentional destruction or concealment of public records
judicial_accountability_council.does_not: Discipline judges merely for disagreement with their decisions.

enforceable_ethics_and_recusal.summary: Go beyond the November 2023 Code of Conduct with enforceable procedures, independent investigation, public disclosure, and external review of contested recusals. A justice should not be the sole and final judge of whether that justice is conflicted.

transparent_emergency_decisions.summary: When the Court blocks or permits a law, stays a lower-court order, or decides a nationally important emergency application, it should generally issue named votes, written reasoning, disclosed recusals, clear duration, and expedited merits review. Emergency procedure should not become an invisible substitute for full adjudication.

public_proceedings.summary: Live audio; archived video where practical; accessible briefs; plain-language summaries; financial and recusal disclosures; searchable voting histories; explanations of procedural dismissals.

removal_paths.title: Impeachment
removal_paths.summary: Preserved for corruption, bribery, abuse of office, serious misconduct, and betrayal of constitutional duty.

removal_paths.title: Judicial Accountability Tribunal
removal_paths.summary: After investigation, the Judicial Accountability Council could recommend removal for severe ethics violations, incapacity, repeated concealed conflicts, or willful disregard of binding ethics requirements — possibly requiring council supermajority, special tribunal review, and two-thirds Senate approval or a national retention vote.

removal_paths.title: National extraordinary retention vote
removal_paths.summary: A justice could be placed before voters only after supermajority council recommendation, substantial multi-state citizen petition support, or concurrent congressional supermajority resolutions. The ballot asks whether the justice should remain based on documented misconduct, incapacity, or breach of public trust — not whether voters like a decision.

ordinary_scotus_recall_rejected.rule: Ordinary partisan recall of Supreme Court justices is rejected.
ordinary_scotus_recall_rejected.reason: It could cause judges to decide cases according to polls, wealthy recall campaigns, or threats from temporary majorities.

constitutional_dialogue.summary: Every branch takes an oath to the Constitution. Courts interpret rights in cases; legislatures may revise statutes; executives may advocate interpretations; citizens may amend; states may test lawful alternatives; the people retain final amendment authority.
when_court_invalidates_law: whether the defect is narrow or fundamental
whether part of the law can survive
whether the decision rests on text, history, precedent, structure, or factual judgment

state_judicial_reform.approach: Standards rather than one compulsory system.
every_state_system_should_include: protection against removal merely for unpopular lawful decisions

mixed_model.trial_judges: Community-based selection with professional qualifications and periodic retention
mixed_model.appellate_judges: Merit selection, fixed terms, public retention, enforceable ethics
mixed_model.state_supreme_court: Long nonrenewable terms, distributed appointment, public retention or structured review
mixed_model.federal_supreme_court: 18-year active terms with independent ethics and extraordinary misconduct removal

anti_wealth_safeguards.rule: A billionaire should not be able to purchase the People’s Branch.
requirements: limits or matching rules considered under constitutional standards
publicly funded argument space for supporters and opponents

federal: direct approval of major constitutional restructuring

citizens_deliberative_assembly.summary: Before major measures reach the ballot, a Citizens’ Deliberative Assembly selected through civic lottery would hear experts and opponents, examine evidence, identify constitutional questions, publish a plain-language report, and recommend approval, rejection, revision, or further study. It would not replace the public vote; it would improve decision quality.

popular_sovereignty_test.purpose: Screen any proposed People’s Branch power, judicial reform, or ballot design.
questions: Does this retain sovereign power in the people without creating a permanent parallel bureaucracy?
Are signature, geographic, disclosure, and deliberation safeguards sufficient to prevent capture by wealth or temporary passion?
Does a hard rights floor prevent majorities from stripping fundamental protections?
Does judicial independence remain strong enough to protect unpopular persons?
Are judges accountable for ethics, conflicts, incapacity, and abuse — without ordinary partisan SCOTUS recall?
Do federal changes clearly identify which steps require constitutional amendment?
Are emergency judicial orders transparent and time-bounded?
Is deliberative process required before major national ballot measures?
